web.title: 30 African Startups That Raised Funding in 2026 (So Far)
web.description:
[Back to Blog](https://startupmaphub.com/blog)

African startups raised **$1.44 billion in the first half of 2026** — slightly ahead of the $1.42 billion raised in H1 2025, but across far fewer deals: just 146 disclosed rounds versus 252 a year earlier. Here are 30 companies that actually got funded this year, and what each deal tells you about where capital is flowing.

The numbers come from [TechCabal Insights](https://insights.techcabal.com/1-44-billion-raised-in-the-first-half-of-2026/), whose trackers put the half-year split at $749 million in Q1 and $692 million in Q2 — $818 million in equity, $614 million in debt and $9 million in grants. [Africa: The Big Deal](https://www.linkedin.com/company/africa-the-big-deal/), which counts only $100k+ deals, tracked $843 million across 160 deals from January to May, split almost evenly between equity and debt — a marked shift from 12–18 months ago, when equity's share sat above 70 percent.

One caveat before the list: not every raise is announced with a press release, and several strong deals this year were undisclosed. Amounts are as disclosed by the companies or tracked by TechCabal Insights, Africa: The Big Deal and our own database.

## All 30 at a glance
| Startup | Country | Sector | Round | 2026 amount |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| Stabyl | Nigeria | Fintech | Pre-seed | $2.7M |

$50M+ • The mega deals

## The growth rounds: debt does the heavy lifting
**GoCab** raised a **$45 million** hybrid round in February — equity from E3 Capital and JANNGO Capital plus significant debt — to scale ride-hailing in Francophone West Africa.

**MAX** raised **$32 million** in equity and asset-backed financing, starting with a $24 million January round, to finance vehicles for commercial drivers and push its fleet electric.

$4M–$15M • Series A & big seeds

## The Series A club — and Morocco's quiet breakout
**WafR** raised a **$4 million seed** in January for retail-tech, and **Enakl** took **$2.3 million** to modernise shared commuting in Casablanca.

Under $3M • Seed & pre-seed

## The early-stage survivors: small cheques, sharp theses
Early-stage equity was the hardest money to raise in 2026 — which makes the companies that closed rounds worth studying.

In AI, Nairobi's **AethexAI** raised a **$3 million pre-seed** led by 4DX Ventures and Enza Capital to build customer-support and voice automation for African markets ( [our full breakdown](https://startupmaphub.com/blog/aethexai-raises-3-million-2026)).

**Zimi Charge** raised **$2.6 million** from the Development Bank of Southern Africa and Keyo Ventures for EV charging in South Africa.

## What these 30 deals tell you about 2026
Half the money went to seven companies; meanwhile 26 startups raised above $100k in January — the lowest tally since at least 2020. If you're raising a $5–15 million round right now, you're in the most competitive segment of the market.

## [Beyond Dialogue: ARCE 2026 Puts Housing Finance, Land Reform and Verified Property Data on Africa’s Real Estate Agenda](https://propertynews.africa/beyond-dialogue-arce-2026-puts-housing-finance-land-reform-and-verified-property-data-on-africas-real-estate-agenda/)
##### About
And African tech funding has just posted its [strongest year since 2022](https://allafrica.com/stories/202601250064.html), even as Nigeria slid down the country rankings.

## Who is coming to Lagos, and what they actually back
SPYRE is India’s first dedicated PropTech venture fund. The fund writes early-stage cheques of ₹2–8 crore and growth cheques of ₹15–40 crore, and aims for a portfolio of 30–35 companies.

Its first R$100 million fund drew capital from homebuilder Cyrela and steelmaker Gerdau, and by late 2024 its 17 portfolio companies had attracted more than R$360 million in total investment. Notably, the firm has been expanding beyond equity into receivables funds and other credit structures — a model with obvious relevance for African PropTechs that finance tenants and buyers.

Zaidan began his career in real estate investment before moving into venture capital in 2016, and previously launched Watheeq Proptech Venture, a US$26.7 million Saudi fund unveiled in 2021 that he describes as the region’s first PropTech-focused VC vehicle.

## The numbers pulling foreign capital toward Nigeria
**Continental funding.** Partech’s annual report counted US$4.1 billion raised by African tech startups in 2025, up 25% and the best year since 2022. PropTech had its landmark moment when Egypt’s Nawy raised US$75 million — a US$52 million Series A led by Partech Africa plus US$23 million in debt from Egyptian banks — the largest PropTech round in African history, which it used to acquire ROA and take a stake in the UAE’s SmartCrowd.

## Room to run: Nigeria’s PropTech breakout is still ahead
Disrupt Africa’s 2025 tracker recorded US$1.64 billion in equity across 178 startups, up 46%, with investors favouring companies that can show revenue and a clear route to profitability.

The first half of 2026 reinforces the point. TechCabal Insights counted US$1.44 billion raised across the continent in H1 2026, with Briter Bridges reporting US$3.3 billion on a broader methodology.

## Snapshot: APPTSUMMIT 2026 and the Nigerian opportunity
| Item | Detail |
|-|-|
| **Real estate in the economy** | Third-largest sector after 2025 rebasing · ₦41.3tn nominal output (2024) · ~10.8% of nominal GDP |
| **African tech funding 2025** | US$4.1bn total (+25%) · US$2.4bn equity · US$1.6bn debt (41% of total) — Partech |

### What this means for African property investors
- **The playbook is proven.** SPYRE (CREDAI, Neovon) and Terracotta (Cyrela, Gerdau) are developer-anchored funds. That template — Nigerian developers seeding a local PropTech vehicle — is the most exportable idea on the agenda.

web.title: Pre-Seed Funding: A Startup's Guide to Early-Stage Fundraising
web.description:
# Pre-seed funding: A startup’s guide to early-stage fundraising
## What is pre-seed funding?
Pre-seed funding is the earliest investment a startup receives. Pre-seed funding is any funding that comes before the seed round.

While there's no single path, data from Carta's [State of Pre-Seed report](https://carta.com/data/state-of-pre-seed-q2-2026/) confirms that founders at this stage typically raise capital from a mix of friends and family, angel investors, and pre-seed venture capitalists (VC). This initial investment happens before a company has a finished product or any revenue.

With early-stage funding, investors are looking for signals that you have a deep understanding of the problem you're trying to solve. They want to see your passion, your unique expertise, and your resilience in the face of early challenges. Your ability to articulate a clear vision is more valuable than any financial projection.

But some companies now raise early priced rounds, which they refer to as pre-seed.

The goal is not to get lost in semantics, but instead provide resources for the type of funding available to early-stage startups, to ultimately help founders find the right investors.

![](https://images.ctfassets.net/y88td1zx1ufe/3n7yznCuZfKbdXx14cEPHZ/2d2bc54a8bec7db41525cdb6f4ee54d1/fundraising-101-cta.png)

Startup Fundraising 101

[Watch now](https://carta.com/learn/startup-fundraising-101/?ir=classroom)

### Pre-seed vs. seed funding
|  |  |  |
|-|-|-|
|  | **Pre-seed round** | **Seed round** |
| **Typical amount raised** | Typically a few hundred thousand dollars (for example, ~$250,000-$1 million), though some rounds are smaller or larger | $500,000-$5 million |
| **Use of funds** | To test your idea | To gain early traction and start selling |

## How much should you raise at a pre-seed round?
There's no universal number, but most pre-seed rounds land between $150,000 and $1 million. [Carta data shows](https://carta.com/data/state-of-pre-seed-q2-2026/) the average instrument is $276,000, with 18% of rounds in the $1–$2.5 million range as of Q1 2026. The right amount is the one that buys you enough runway to hit your next set of milestones.

Aim for 12-24 months of runway. That's usually the window you need to build a product, validate demand, and reach the traction that leads to a seed round. Raise too little and you'll be back out fundraising before you have results to show. Raise too much and you may give away more ownership than the stage warrants.

Current data can anchor your target. In Q2 2026, the average pre-seed instrument on Carta was $276,000, a record high and up 27% year over year, according to Carta's [State of Pre-Seed report](https://carta.com/data/state-of-pre-seed-q2-2026/). Few pre-seed deals exceed $2.5 million, at least in the U.S., so a round in the low-to-mid six figures is well within the norm.

List the milestones that make you fundable at seed, such as a shipped MVP, early users, and key hires, then estimate the cost and timeline to reach them. Add a buffer for the fundraising process itself, which can take months. The figure you land on is your target raise, grounded in a plan rather than a round-number guess.

![](https://images.ctfassets.net/y88td1zx1ufe/6xJ0yc90rSyFndvy9DNQQm/e6e1b1bb2a88caaf12fec91300003b81/Data_minute_benchmark_for_web.png)

[Get started](https://carta.com/data/explore/round-benchmarking/?ir=classroom)

## How to get pre-seed funding
Getting ready for your pre-seed round is about more than just having a good idea.

Raising a pre-seed round requires more than a good idea.

![Saudi proptech Ghanem raises $1.5 million pre-seed extension](https://cdn.wamda.com/feature-images/ac6c827930ca77b.jpg)

- Saudi Arabia-based proptech startup Ghanem has raised an additional $1.5 million in a pre-seed extension round, backed by real estate companies and strategic angel investors, bringing the round's total to $8.6 million. Its previous [$7.1 million financing](https://www.wamda.com/index.php/2025/11/saudi-proptech-ghanem-raises-7-1-million-al-romaih-group) included participation from Al-Romaih Group, while Waad VC has also invested in the company.
- The additional funding will support product development, diversification of property investment opportunities and strategic partnerships, as the company expands its fractional ownership services.

**Press release:**

The funding extends the company’s pre-seed round, which previously raised $7.1 million with participation from Al-Romaih Group, bringing the total round, including the extension, to $8.6 million. Waad VC has also invested in the company.

These include the execution of several real estate investment transactions through the company, a registered user base now numbering in the thousands, and the start of rental income distributions to investors without any payment disruptions.

Ghanem successfully issued digital ownership deeds to 580 individuals participating in the first income-generating real estate investment opportunity offered through the Ghanem app, documenting their fractional ownership stakes in the property.

Saleh Waheed Al-Ghamdi, CEO and Co-Founder of Ghanem, said, "We are working to make property ownership more accessible through a clear digital experience and ownership documented in the investor’s name. We have executed real estate investment transactions, distributed monthly dividends with zero delays, attracted thousands of registered users, and activated our digital integration with the Real Estate Registry.

Al-Ghamdi added, "This pre-seed extension provides important support for the next stage of our journey. We value our investors’ trust and the participation of real estate companies and strategic partners with direct market experience.

A faster way to raise a first round is to start with the best pre-seed funds that have just announced new capital, because these firms have money available and a clear plan for how many companies they want to back.

Every fund on this list announced fresh capital in August 2026 and is ready to invest in pre-seed or seed startups.

## **What Are Pre-Seed Funds?**
Pre-seed funds are venture firms that write the first institutional checks into a startup, usually before the company has meaningful revenue. The money typically pays for building an early product, hiring the first few people and gathering the proof that a seed investor will want to see later.

Pre-seed rounds are usually raised through SAFEs and convertible notes, and in 2026 the rounds generally range from $250K to $1.5M.

According to Carta, the average pre-seed instrument reached $276,000 in Q2 2026, a 27% increase from the year before and a record high in more than four years.

Carta's [State of Pre-Seed report](https://carta.com/data/state-of-pre-seed-q2-2026/) also shows that AI companies captured 49% of all pre-seed dollars in the first half of 2026, which explains why so many funds on this list mention AI in their focus.

Pre-seed investors mostly evaluate the founding team, the size of the market and any early signal of demand, such as a waitlist, a pilot or a set of customer interviews.

## **Best Pre-Seed Funds in the Rest of the World**
### **24. Ventures Platform Fund**
**Fund Size:** $84M
